label: Bible Study
prompt: Strength and honour are her _____; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
verse: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
note: From the virtuous woman poem — dressed in strength and honour, and laughing at the future.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And in the wilderness, where thou hast seen how that the LORD thy God bare thee, as a man doth bear his _____, in all the way that ye went, until ye came into this place.
verse: And in the wilderness, where thou hast seen how that the LORD thy God bare thee, as a man doth bear his son, in all the way that ye went, until ye came into this place.
note: Through the wilderness God carried Israel 'as a man doth bear his son' — every step of the way.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Behold the _____ of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
verse: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
note: The KJV's 'fowls of the air' are just birds — no barns, no savings plan, and fed every day anyway.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the _____ for our sins.
verse: Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.
note: John defines love by propitiation — the sacrifice that turns away wrath — so it's no minor word.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God _____!
verse: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!
note: Hired to curse Israel, Balaam blessed instead: 'What hath God wrought!' — later the first message on Morse's telegraph line, 1844.
